name: Treaty with the Creeks, 1818 (Treaty of the Creek Agency)
promises: Article 2: for the two tracts ceded in Article 1, the United States would pay $120,000 in eleven instalments without interest: $20,000 within the year and $10,000 a year for the ten years after.
Article 3: two blacksmiths and strikers for the Creek Nation for three years.
Article 4: the President could have any needed boundary line run.
today: No Indian Claims Commission, Court of Claims or other federal finding about this cession or its payments was found in this pass.

sources.title: Treaty with the Creeks, 1818 (Kappler, Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties, vol. 2)
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 688

openQuestions: Whether the eleven instalments under Article 2 were all paid was not traced. A War Department letter of 1818 in the Digital Library of Georgia reportedly concerns annuities under the treaties of 1805 and 1818; it was not opened.
The Creek dockets in the Indian Claims Commission collection do not appear to cover this cession; a deeper pass could check the Commission's 1978 Final Report docket list.
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation's own account of this treaty was not found in this pass.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Creek (Court of Claims index, every case 1919 to 1943 grepped for 1818 and 7 Stat. 171) and 'Creek 1818 Creek Agency', 'Creek January 22 1818' (ICC); nothing on this cession.
